spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Kephalaia
 Passage


**
¶7.
** It
 is right
 that you perce
ive this in
ward
ly. The external
 tru
ths called
 "great"
 are the five essential
 faculties of the
 rational mind —
 understanding, reflection, perception, discern
ment, and resolve
 —
 which complete and
 perfect the regener
ated spiritual person,
 who
 is the Divine
 Human in
 form
. These fac
ulties were purified and
 made
 transl
ucent by the infl
owing
 of the Divine
 itself
 into
 the mind
.


**¶8.** By
 contrast, what
 are called "rags" — that
 is
, fragmentary and
 t
attered truths —
 are the scattered
 remn
ants of divine wisdom
 that
 have been sw
allowed up,

ounded, and entangled within
 the whole
 natural
 order
 of
 the
 mind
:
 in
 the
 dominant
 falsities that
 rule
 from
 above, existing
 across
 all the
 fixed
 doctrinal frameworks.
 Their
 resid
ual lumin
osity is what
 still
 gl
immers
 and
 shows
 itself
 in the isolated
 kn
owledges of good
 and truth,
 and
 in the governing
 influences
 of
 natural
 thought
's
 recurring
 course
.
 And likewise
, these fragment
ary tru
ths are
 entangled within
 the three degrees
 of the natural mind below
 —
 above
 the sust
aining principle at
 the foundation, and
 in
 the ou
termost natural
 plane
 beneath
 that
 sust
aining principle.
 These are called "rags" because
 they have
 been torn
 from
 their whol
eness and dispers
ed.


**¶9.** The
 tru
ths called "great but
 worn
 through
 and
 torn
 apart" are
 the living divine
 power
 itself
 —
 truth
 still
 vital
 —
 which has been harv
ested, sev
ered, and consumed.
 It has
 been ov
erpowered by the five orders
 of the prop
rium, the
 self
-derived life
 of
 the
 flesh:
 self
-love
, love
 of the world
, sens
ory
 cr
aving, bod
ily appetite
, and rest
less desire
 —
 which cre
ep and
 shift
 ce
aselessly from one
 object
 to another,
 never
 at
 rest.

**¶10.
** What
 are called "li
kenesses and
 great tattered cov
erings" are the three foundational external
 truths:
 truth
 of
 thought
,
 truth
 of love's
 ard
or, and truth of understanding
's
 flow
 — corresponding
 to wind
, fire, and water. With
 these the
 Lord
 as
 Divine
 operative truth clothed his
 active
 presence.
 Through
 them he
 brought
 all
 things of
 the mind
 into order
.
 Through them also
 he emptied the containing forms
 of
 the natural
 mind
, swept
 them clean
, and laid them bare before the sust
aining principle at the foundation of all things
 —
 so
 that they
 might receive
 what
 is
 divine
 without
 obst
ruction.

**¶11.
** What
 are called "elements" are the resid
ual divine power that
 remains lat
ent in all things
 of
 the lowest
 natural
 degree
.
 It rises up
ward through the receptive inter
iors of every
 level
 of the natural
 mind
, g
athers itself
 together, and pours itself forth upon
 all things —
 as
 the Lord's life
 contin
ually p
resses
 up
ward even
 through
 what
 is most
 external
.

**¶12.**
 What is
 called the
 "Cross
 of
 Wisdom" is this
 same
 divine
 truth
-
and
-good,
 bound
 and
 fixed
 within
 the natural plane
 — extending
 through
 all conditions
 of
 the earth
ly mind
, in states
 that
 are bar
ren of
 truth and in
 states that are receptive to
 it
,
 in what
 is dry and in
 what is moist.

**
¶13.** What is called the
 "counsel of life" is the divine
 calling and the will's ob
edient response.
 It moves within
 all the
 powers named
 above
.
 It awakens them from
 dorm
ancy, brings
 them into
 peace, and impels them toward their
 proper spiritual motion —
 which
 is the
 return
 toward
 their
 origin
.


**¶14.** What
 is called "
the soul that is slain" —
 which
 is killed
, oppressed, and destroyed
 — is the divine good and truth residing
 in works, in
 natural goods, and in interior truths
 still
 in
 seed
.
 These
 are th
reshed, plucked up
, and cut down;
 and
 they give sust
enance to the self
-derived orders
 of the flesh,
 which
 consume
 them
 for
 their own life
.
 Furthermore
:
 perception
,
 when
 it becomes
 bar
ren of truth —
 like
 dry wood — and external
 truth
, when it becomes so
 degrad
ed that it can
 no longer cloth
e the mind —
 like
 a
 ragged garment — will perish
 entirely
. This
 too
 is part of that
 same
 whole
 divine
 life which
 is profaned and destroyed
;
 for
 every
 portion
 of it that
 enters
 the natural
,
 they
 kill.

**¶15.
** All these names — r
ags, worn
 gar
ments, t
attered coverings, elements
, the
 cross
 of
 bound
 wisdom,
 the counsel of life, the sl
ain soul — are a single divine wisdom
.
 From
 the beginning it was one
, and
 as
 one
 it illumin
ated
 all things. But in the first spiritual
 conflict —
 when evil
 rose
 against
 good and
 fals
ity against truth — that
 unity
 was divided
 into
 all these separated
 conditions
. It
 became fixed in all these altered forms and
 received
 these
 many names. Yet
 if now
 all these varieties are laid
 bare, and stripped of every
 out
ward appearance, and freed
 from every distingu
ishing name, they will gather together and
 become
 again
 a single form and a single essence
 —
 un
altered and unchangeable forever
 in the kingdom
 of their first origin
, from which they were sent forth against
 the enemy.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: “It is proper for you to understand this. The garments that are named ‘great garment’ are the five intellectuals that make perfect the body of the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. They were purified by the coming of the Ambassador.

“In contrast, the ones named ‘rag’: the rags are the devoured enlightening power. It is compounded and entangled in the body of the universe in the rulers who are above, who exist in all the firmaments. Also, its shine is that which lights up and is displayed in the stars of the chain and the powers of the course. And likewise, these rags that are entangled in these three earths below, above the head of the Porter [...] on the earth that is under the Porter. These are named the ‘rags’, because [...] set [...]

“However, the ‘great worn and torn apart garments’, which we have proclaimed, is this entangled living power. It is reaped, cut, and devoured. It is overpowered by the five worlds of the flesh, which creep as they move from place to place.

“On the other hand, [these] we have termed the ‘images and the great tattered clothes’ [...] are the three great garments of the wind, the fire, and the water. These the Living Spirit cloaked upon his body. With them he set in order things in the universe. With them also he emptied the vessels. He swept them out and laid them bare in front of the Porter at the foundation of all things.

“Conversely, ‘[the ele]ments’, we have called them this name, are this power that remains in all things below. It rises up in the wombs of all the earths, gathering together, and pouring forth upon all things.
“And then, the ‘[Light] Cross’ [we have termed] this bound ‘light power’. It [...] all [...] upon the earth, in the dry and the moist.
“Also, the one named the ‘counsel of life’ is the summons and the obedience. It moves in all these powers that we have named. It awakens them, gives them ease, and drives them to their movement.

“The one named ‘the soul that is slain’, which is killed, oppressed and murdered; it is this power of fruit, vegetables and seeds. They shall be threshed, plucked and cut down; and they give nourishment to the worlds of the flesh. Further: the wood should it be dry, and the garment should it become ragged, will perish. Again, it is [a pa]rt of this entire soul that is slain and killed; since also even this whole part of it they kill [...]
